$comment: Keiko Editor bundle-size budget (Issue #1207; ADR-0042 D3.6). Enforced deterministically by scripts/editor-bundle-size.mjs, which runs standalone (`npm run check:editor-bundle-size`) and inside `check:package-surface` (the `ci` prepack chain). PR CI for feat/keiko-editor also runs it after `npm run build:ui` with `--require-static-export` so initial static-export JS is scanned. The 2.5 MB-gzip lazy editor + Monaco runtime budget and the <=750 KB-gzip per-worker-chunk budget are measured against the real production bundle as release evidence by #1209; this file enforces the parts that regress in this repo deterministically: the editor package's own compiled footprint, the pinned Monaco version the runtime footprint was measured against, and the first-load code-split isolation (Monaco/editor runtime value-imported only behind a client-only dynamic boundary). The 316 KiB initial-page ceiling records the rebased #2055 + #1982 desktop baseline, rebased for Epic #2238 (governed Atlassian connector UI), and rebased again (315392 -> 323584, +8 KiB) for the PR #2315 i18n retrofit of six previously-uncovered Quality/Files widgets (AgentRunWidget, FilePreview, FilesWidget, PdfCitationPreviewWindow, ReviewWidget, FigmaSnapshotWindow): its user-facing strings live in the eagerly-loaded central English i18n catalog (required by check:ui-i18n), which is first-load state, while the connector/widget components themselves are code-split behind their own routes. The ceiling is set from the CI/Linux-measured static-export footprint (319780 B observed) with ~4 KiB margin for macOS-vs-Linux gzip variance (CI/Linux is the authoritative measurement), following the same +4 KiB-increment convention as the two prior rebases, while preserving a tight regression guard. See docs/keiko-editor/1207-performance-budgets.md.
